life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are
fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

crossings which are potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.areaDesc: Yukon Delta Coast
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 22 at 2:18PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
We are currently tracking a low that is expected to move through
the southern Bering Sea Thursday through Saturday and which could
approach the coast of the Yukon Delta. While the most likely
storm track south of our area would result in only modest rises in
above normal high water for the Yukon Delta, a further north
track could result in high surf potential. As of right now, the
southern portion of the Yukon Delta coast could see water levels
rise to around 1 to 3 feet above the mean high water line, with
rises more likely to be on the lower side of that range. We will
continue to monitor this system closely.

NWSheadline: HIGH SURF POTENTIAL FOR YUKON DELTA COAST TOWARD END OF THE WEEK

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued September 22 at 1:36PM AKDT until September 26 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Water levels on average of 1 to 2 feet above the normal
highest tide line. Southeast winds 35 to 45 mph with gusts up to
60 mph expected Thursday. South winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts to
50 mph expected Friday.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast including Kwigillingok and Kipnuk.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Thursday to 4 AM Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There will be multiple peaks in water
levels for the Kuskokwim Delta Thursday morning through Saturday
morning coinciding with high tide cycles and strong southerly
winds. Southeast winds 35 to 45 mph with gusts to 60 mph
Thursday afternoon will diminish early Friday until the low
pressure system moves west of the coast by Friday afternoon.
Then, winds will become southerly at 30 to 40 mph with gusts to
50 mph by Friday afternoon. Winds gradually weaken but remain
southerly through Saturday.

For Kwigillingok, water levels reach 1 to 2 feet above the
normal highest tide line on Thursday, coinciding with the passage
of a frontal system. Water levels could reach up to 4 feet in a
worst case scenario.

For Kipnuk, the highest water levels of 1 to 2 feet above the
normal highest tide line are expected on Friday as a low pressure
system moves west of the coast and winds become southerly. Water
levels could reach 2 to 3 feet in a worst case scenario.

For more information regarding potential local flood impacts,
please reference maps.dggs.alaska.gov/akfit/
properties.instruction:
A coastal flood watch means that conditions favorable for
flooding are expected to develop. Coastal residents should be
alert for later statements or warnings, and take action to
protect property.

properties.description:
At 327 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.25 inches are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

you encounter flood waters, climb to safety.

properties.areaDesc: Interior Kuskokwim Delta
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 22 at 12:43PM AKDT until September 26 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Interior Kuskokwim Delta, including Kwethluk, Kasigluk,
Bethel, Napaskiak, Napakiak, Oscarville, and other nearby villages.

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rain in combination of persistent high water
levels and storm surge may result in flooding of rivers, creeks,
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Creeks and
streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Area creeks and streams are running high and could flood
with more heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A strong storm projected to move into the eastern Bering Sea will
bring heavy rainfall and storm surge to the area. The Kuskokwim
River is currently running high, with statistics showing the
river is already above the 90th percentile in flow for this time
of year. 1 to 2 inches of rainfall across the Kilbuck Mountains,
as well as across the lower Kuskokwim, is likely to exacerbate
high water levels for the Kwethluk River, Johnson River / tundra
villages, as well as other smaller tributaries and sloughs of the
Kuskokwim.

Confidence is moderate-to-high that flooding of low-lying areas
will occur for Kwethluk and Kasigluk, where high-water was
reported last week. Confidence is lower for flooding elsewhere
and will be dependent on the rainfall amount and degree of
compounding effects from coastal surge and tide cycle.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued September 22 at 4:42PM EDT until September 23 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Strong longshore currents in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Crystal Coast beaches.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Strong longshore currents will create dangerous
swimming conditions.
properties.instruction:
Strong longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip
currents, piers, jetties and other hazardous areas. In many
cases, the longshore current is strong enough to prevent swimmers
from being able to keep their feet on the bottom making it
difficult to return to shore.

properties.areaDesc: Ocracoke Island
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued September 22 at 4:42PM EDT until September 23 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and strong longshore currents in the surf zone. For the Coastal
Flood Warning, 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.
Up to 1 foot of inundation is possible for sound-side flooding
when winds become more northerly late Thursday and Friday.

* WHERE...Ocracoke Island.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Wednesday morning
through Wednesday evening. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from
2 PM Wednesday to 11 PM EDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Portions of Highway 12
will be inundated. Low lying property including homes,
businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
Some shoreline erosion will occur. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. Strong
longshore currents will create dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Prolonged nature of the event will continue
to erode dune structures. Winds and waves are forecast to peak
latter half of Thursday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 22 at 2:25PM MDT until September 22 at 5:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 225 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.75 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Vermejo Park.

High water flows are expected in the Canadian River. Stay away from
river banks.
properties.instruction:
In hilly or mountainous terrain there are numerous low water
crossings which are potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

Do not enter or cross flowing water or water of unknown depth.

properties.areaDesc: Eastern Monmouth
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 22 at 4:14PM EDT until September 25 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 12
feet expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
up to one foot of inundation above ground level expected in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Eastern Monmouth.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Wednesday to
6 PM EDT Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 PM
Wednesday to 1 AM EDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along
inland tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are
possible. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Widespread minor tidal flooding could
continue through at least Friday evening's high tide or perhaps
longer.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Always obey posted Beach Flags. If you enter the surf zone,
always have a floatation device with you and swim near a
lifeguard if possible. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float and do not swim against the current. If able, swim parallel
to the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or
wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Randolph, WV; Webster, WV
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 22 at 4:11PM EDT until September 22 at 7:00PM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
FFWRLX

The National Weather Service in Charleston has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Randolph County in northeastern West Virginia...
Northern Webster County in northeastern West Virginia...

* Until 700 PM EDT.

* At 411 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2.5 inches of rain
have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Webster Springs, Addison (Webster Springs), Waneta, Bergoo, Pickens
and Monterville.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

properties.areaDesc: Southern Nassau
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued September 22 at 3:19PM EDT until September 23 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Statement, up to one half foot of
inundation above ground level expected in vulnerable areas
near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...Southern Nassau County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Wednesday
evening. For the Coastal Flood Statement, from Wednesday
afternoon through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Brief minor flooding of the more vulnerable
locations near the waterfront and shoreline. Life-
threatening rip currents are likely for all people entering
the surf zone. Anyone visiting the beaches should stay out of
the surf. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The high rip current risk is expected to
persist through late week.
properties.instruction:
Do not drive through flooded roadways.

If you enter the surf zone, always have a flotation device with
you and swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax
and float, and do not swim against the current. If able, swim in
a direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face
the shore and yell or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Athens, OH
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 22 at 3:07PM EDT until September 23 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Charleston has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Ohio...

Hocking River at Athens affecting Athens County.

For the Hocking River...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Hocking River at Athens.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to late tonight.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Low sections of Harmony Road begin to
flood. In Nelsonville, the baseball fields along Watkins Street
flood. At 20.0 feet, Low areas, campground, and private camps along
the river between Athens and Coolville begin to flood. Much of the
city of Athens is protected up to 26 feet by levees. In
Nelsonville, the baseball field adjacent to Lake Hope Drive floods.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:15 PM EDT Tuesday the stage was 20.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 16.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:15 PM EDT Tuesday was 20.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
this evening and continue falling to 10.9 feet Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 20.1
feet on 02/10/2019.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/rlx.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 315 AM EDT.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 22 at 2:57PM EDT until September 23 at 4:00PM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement,a high risk of rip
currents is expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one
foot of inundation above ground level expected in low-lying
areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf
Advisory, large breaking waves of 9 to 13 feet expected in the
surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Warning, one to two feet of
inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...In Maryland, Maryland Beaches County. In Virginia,
Accomack and Northampton Counties.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Wednesday
evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM EDT
Wednesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 2 AM Wednesday to
6 PM EDT Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 PM
Wednesday to 4 AM EDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. Dangerous
swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Anne Arundel
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued September 22 at 2:53PM EDT until September 25 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Baltimore MD/Washington DC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, around one and a half
feet of inundation above ground level in low lying areas due to
tidal flooding. For the Coastal Flood Watch, two to two and a
half feet of inundation above ground level possible in low
lying areas due to tidal flooding.

* WHERE...Shoreline in Anne Arundel County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until midnight EDT
Wednesday night, especially around the time of high tide. For
the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Wednesday night through
late Thursday night, especially around the time of high tide.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, water reaches the floor of the Maritime
Museum in Annapolis, begins to cover Bowyer Road on the Naval
Academy campus, and numerous businesses on Dock Street are
flooded, along with the City Dock parking lot. Bayside Beach
begins to flood around Harbor Rd and Lake Dr.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tides two to two and a half feet above
normal. The next high tide at Annapolis U.S. Naval Academy is at
3:31 AM and 3:33 PM.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Northwest Plateau; Chuska Mountains; Far Northwest Highlands; Northwest Highlands; West Central Plateau; West Central Mountains; West Central Highlands; Southwest Mountains; San Francisco River Valley; Tusas Mountains Including Chama; Jemez Mountains; Glorieta Mesa Including Glorieta Pass; Northern Sangre de Cristo Mountains; Southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains; East Slopes Sangre de Cristo Mountains; Upper Rio Grande Valley; Espanola Valley; Santa Fe Metro Area; Middle Rio Grande Valley/Albuquerque Metro Area; Lower Rio Grande Valley; Sandia/Manzano Mountains Including Edgewood; Estancia Valley; Central Highlands; South Central Highlands; Upper Tularosa Valley; South Central Mountains; Johnson and Bartlett Mesas Including Raton Pass; Far Northeast Highlands; Northeast Highlands; Union County; Harding County; Eastern San Miguel County; Guadalupe County; Quay County; De Baca County; Chaves County Plains; Eastern Lincoln County; Southwest Chaves County; San Agustin Plains and Adjacent Lowlands
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 22 at 11:57AM MDT until September 24 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, north central,
northeast, northwest, southeast, and west central New Mexico,
including the following areas, in central New Mexico, Central
Highlands, Eastern Lincoln County, Estancia Valley, Lower Rio
Grande Valley, Middle Rio Grande Valley including the Albuquerque
Metro Area, San Agustin Plains and Adjacent Lowlands, Sandia and
Manzano Mountains including Edgewood, South Central Highlands,
South Central Mountains and Upper Tularosa Valley. In east central
New Mexico, De Baca County, Guadalupe County and Quay County. In
north central New Mexico, East Slopes Sangre de Cristo Mountains,
Espanola Valley, Far Northwest Highlands, Glorieta Mesa Including
Glorieta Pass, Jemez Mountains, Northern Sangre de Cristo
Mountains, Northwest Highlands, Santa Fe Metro Area, Southern
Sangre de Cristo Mountains, Tusas Mountains Including Chama and
Upper Rio Grande Valley. In northeast New Mexico, Eastern San
Miguel County, Far Northeast Highlands, Harding County, Johnson and
Bartlett Mesas Including Raton Pass, Northeast Highlands and Union
County. In northwest New Mexico, Chuska Mountains and Northwest
Plateau. In southeast New Mexico, Chaves County Plains and
Southwest Chaves County. In west central New Mexico, San Francisco
River Valley, Southwest Mountains, West Central Highlands, West
Central Mountains and West Central Plateau.

* WHEN...Through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.
Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A dangerous surge of monsoon moisture will arrive today and
Wednesday with widespread heavy rain.  Scattered occurrences of
flash flooding are likely, and there will probably be some main
stem river and tributary flooding later in the week, as the most
likely rain amount by Wednesday afternoon exceeds 1.5 inches many
locations along and east of the central mountain chain, and 1
inch in many locations westward to around Dulce, Gallup, and
Glenwood. Stronger storms will produce torrential rainfall at
rates over 2 inches per hour, and storms will train repeatedly in
succession over some locations, with locally heavier rain amounts
reaching over 4 inches over portions of southern, central, and
eastern New Mexico.  Heavy rain will likely continue Wednesday
night over north-central and eastern New Mexico, then showers and
storms with locally heavy rainfall are forecast to return to much
of the state again on Thursday.
- Rapid runoff and flash flooding will be most likely in complex
terrain, below recent burn scars, low-lying areas, urban areas,
normally dry arroyos, and near rivers and streams.  As the event
unfolds, locations with saturated ground will also become prone
to rapid runoff and flash flooding from additional rounds of
storms.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

areas, San Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,

thunderstorms are expected Wednesday through Thursday evening

July, and on September 15 reached flood stage. The cause of the high

hydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a

hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing water
levels to rise.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 22 at 8:07AM EDT until September 22 at 9:00PM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Central Athens County in southeastern Ohio...
Southwestern Morgan County in southeastern Ohio...
Northeastern Vinton County in southeastern Ohio...
West Central Washington County in southeastern Ohio...

* WHEN...Until 900 PM EDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 806 AM EDT, local law enforcement reported flooding was
continuing across much of the county from previous heavy rains.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Athens, Nelsonville, Lake Hope State Park, Chauncey, Buchtel,
Amesville, The Plains and Stroud Run State Park.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

properties.areaDesc: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 22 at 4:48PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
An active monsoon pattern will continue across western Micronesia
with satellite imagery continuing to show areas of heavy showers and
thunderstorms. Latest satellite-dervied surface wind data depicts 15
to 20 mph west to southwest winds across western Yap State and Palau
with pockets of locally higher winds.

Weather models point to a continuation of these conditions with
periods of locally heavy showers moving across the islands,
occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts, and choppy seas. Both
Yap and Palau are in the monsoon inflow of Invest 91W, located near
13N142E, northeast of Yap. 91W is now the subject of a Tropical
Cyclone Formation Alert from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center and
showers are expected to remain mostly numerous to widespread and
heavy at times. Model guidance suggests 1 to 3 inches of rain per day
will be possible through Wednesday, especially for Yap.

Residents should continue to monitor forecasts and listen for any
marine advisories that may be issued over the next couple of days.
Be aware of the latest weather conditions and trends before traveling
between islands. Stay up-to-date with all the latest forecasts at
weather.gov/gum and by following the latest information from your
local Weather Service Office.

NWSheadline: LOCALLY HEAVY SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS YAP STATE AND PALAU THROUGH WEDNESDAY... ...PERIODIC GUSTY WEST TO SOUTHWEST WINDS THROUGH FRIDAY

properties.areaDesc: Majuro Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 22 at 4:12PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Conditions have generally tapered down across Majuro from yesterdays
wind and rain event. Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms
will bring some locally heavy showers through tonight. Further north,
a tropical disturbance has produced robust convection across Bikini
Atoll and the far northern Marshall Islands today. This morning's
scatterometer shows that gusts could be approaching 40 to 45 knots in
the heaviest showers and thunderstorms. Some of this heavy weather
has made it as far south of Kwajalein today. Over the next couple of
days, model guidance shows a westward shift of the tropical
disturbance with a slow weakening trend. Scattered showers will
remain possible across the RMI this week with a monsoon-like pattern
remaining in place.

Seas could approach 9 to 12 feet where the strongest winds and
heaviest showers occur. This would make conditions hazardous to
Small Craft across the far northern RMI with extreme choppiness.
Boaters moving through the Marshall Islands north of Kwajalein
should practice enhanced caution over the next day or so.

For more information keep up to date with the latest information
from the Majuro Weather Service office and your local emergency
management agency.

NWSheadline: VERY HEAVY RAINFALL AND GUSTY WINDS ACROSS BIKINI ATOLL AND THE FAR NORTHERN MARSHALL ISLANDS THROUGH TONIGHT

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 21 at 3:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
We are currently tracking a low that is expected to move through
the southern Bering Sea Thursday through Saturday and which could
approach the coast of the YK Delta. While the most likely storm
track south of our area would result in only modest rises in above
normal high water, a further north track could result in high
surf potential. As of right now, the southern portion of the YK
Delta coast could see water levels rise to around 1 to 3 feet
above the mean high water line. We will continue to monitor this
system closely.

NWSheadline: HIGH SURF POTENTIAL FOR YUKON DELTA COAST TOWARD END OF THE WEEK
